body: Hong Kong's newly revamped Huanggang Port is preparing for a significant increase in passenger traffic during the upcoming three-day Chung Yeung Festival holiday. Officials expect the port to handle more than 100,000 passenger trips per day.
Despite the anticipated rush, the departure hall was quiet on Saturday morning. However, the port has seen consistent operations since its opening on Monday.

articles.dek: Five yachts from mainland China have arrived in Hong Kong, marking the first arrivals under a relaxed cross-border maritime scheme aimed at facilitating leisure boat travel.

articles.takeaway: Five yachts from mainland China have arrived in Hong Kong, marking the first arrivals under a relaxed cross-border maritime scheme aimed at facilitating leisure boat travel.
body: Five yachts registered in Guangdong province have sailed into Hong Kong, becoming the first vessels to do so under a new scheme that eases requirements for leisure boats from mainland China.

The flotilla, comprising three boats from Shenzhen, one from Zhuhai, and one from Guangzhou, arrived on Friday and berthed at Lantau Yacht Club. They were greeted with a horn salute from Marine Department vessels.

Hong Kong authorities began accepting applications from Guangdong yacht operators earlier this week. The new scheme permits southbound skippers to seek shelter in five designated anchorages in Hong Kong, with a total capacity for approximately 115 vessels up to 40 meters in length.

This initiative follows an agreement between Hong Kong and Guangdong authorities in late September to implement cross-boundary yacht travel. Previously, significant financial deposits and lengthy licensing processes were required for yacht owners crossing the maritime boundary.

He has been clinically assessed as requiring an immediate liver transplant and is currently listed as the top priority for an O+ blood group liver. The HA is urging the public to consider organ donation, particularly from deceased relatives, for critically ill patients.

articles.headline: Hong Kong to Launch Central Gold Clearing Platform Next Year
articles.dek: The city aims to establish itself as a global gold hub by developing a comprehensive trading ecosystem, with government backing and cross-border cooperation as key differentiators.
articles.lead: Hong Kong is set to launch a central gold clearing platform in the first quarter of next year, aiming to bolster its position as a global gold trading hub. Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui Ching-yu stated that the platform will handle both physical delivery and payments, integrating with the real-time gross settlement system.
articles.takeaway: The city aims to establish itself as a global gold hub by developing a comprehensive trading ecosystem, with government backing and cross-border cooperation as key differentiators.
body: Hong Kong is set to launch a central gold clearing platform in the first quarter of next year, aiming to bolster its position as a global gold trading hub. Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui Ching-yu stated that the platform will handle both physical delivery and payments, integrating with the real-time gross settlement system.

The initiative is part of Hong Kong's first five-year plan, which seeks to create an international gold and precious metals trading ecosystem covering the entire value chain. This includes trading, storage, clearing, refining, and risk management, with a focus on the Asian time zone.

Key features distinguishing Hong Kong's approach from London include government ownership and backing of the clearing house, integrated delivery-versus-payment settlement, and cooperation with Shanghai. This cross-border arrangement will allow eligible gold stored in Hong Kong to be used for settling trades in both markets.

The government plans to increase Hong Kong's gold storage capacity to over 2,000 tonnes within three years. Additionally, plans are underway to relaunch a US dollar-denominated gold futures contract, with details of a yuan-denominated contract to be announced by year-end.

Hui expressed confidence in Hong Kong's competitive advantages, emphasizing that a successful commodities market requires proximity to the real economy, encompassing logistics and storage alongside financial trading. An industry association is also expected to be established by the end of the year.

articles.dek: Terence Arnold joins the Court of Final Appeal as an overseas non-permanent judge amid a series of departures from the bench.
articles.lead: New Zealand judge Terence Arnold has been appointed as an overseas non-permanent judge to Hong Kong's Court of Final Appeal (CFA). The appointment follows the recent death of Australian judge William Gummow and a series of resignations by other foreign jurists.
articles.takeaway: Terence Arnold joins the Court of Final Appeal as an overseas non-permanent judge amid a series of departures from the bench.
body: New Zealand judge Terence Arnold has been appointed as an overseas non-permanent judge to Hong Kong's Court of Final Appeal (CFA). The appointment follows the recent death of Australian judge William Gummow and a series of resignations by other foreign jurists.

Arnold's appointment, effective Friday, will be presented to the Legislative Council for approval. He joins five other foreign judges from common law jurisdictions currently serving on the CFA. Hong Kong's Chief Justice Andrew Cheung welcomed the decision, which was based on a recommendation from the Judicial Officers Recommendation Commission.

Hong Kong leader John Lee stated that the presence of six overseas jurists demonstrates the independence of the judiciary and maintains strong links with other common law jurisdictions. He added that their participation signifies confidence in the HKSAR's judicial system.

Arnold, who has served on New Zealand's Supreme Court since 2013, retired from its permanent bench in 2017 but continues to sit as a retired judge. He previously held the position of Solicitor-General of New Zealand from 2000 to 2006.

The judiciary indicated that Arnold's appointment will offer greater flexibility in managing the court's caseload. This appointment occurs against a backdrop of several foreign judges leaving the CFA, with some citing concerns about the political environment and the role of overseas judges.

articles.headline: Hong Kong teen makes cents of finance, taps AI to tackle economic inequality
articles.dek: At 17, Hong Kong secondary school student Agastya Rekhi has been teaching finance and economics to younger children for nearly three years. Meeting families struggling to understand how prices, investments and economic…
articles.lead: At 17, Hong Kong secondary school student Agastya Rekhi has been teaching finance and economics to younger children for nearly three years. Meeting families struggling to understand how prices, investments and economic news impacted their daily lives during voluntary work convinced him that access to information was only part of the problem.
articles.takeaway: At 17, Hong Kong secondary school student Agastya Rekhi has been teaching finance and economics to younger children for nearly three years.
body: At 17, Hong Kong secondary school student Agastya Rekhi has been teaching finance and economics to younger children for nearly three years. Meeting families struggling to understand how prices, investments and economic news impacted their daily lives during voluntary work convinced him that access to information was only part of the problem.

How that information was communicated was just as important. Rekhi, a finalist for the Spirit of Youth Award in this year’s Spirit of Hong Kong Awards, has since launched three student-led projects spanning financial education, simplified economic news and AI support for smaller organisations.

He started Launchpad at 14, leveraging his interests in games and art to teach economics, business and financial literacy to children. Rekhi said the project has held about 105 sessions, reaching 215 students across Hong Kong, India and the United Kingdom.

Instead of relying on textbooks, lessons turn economic concepts into activities. For example, the concept of the “tragedy of the commons”, coined by American ecologist Garrett Hardin to describe how overusing shared resources causes collective ruin, was taught through a game in which children shared a plate of marshmallows using chopsticks.

Through this, students learned how taking too many out of self-interest left fewer shared resources for everyone else. Rekhi said the intention was to make concepts that can appear intimidating more familiar, particularly for children who may not grow up discussing money or investing at home.
“Financial literacy is often thought of as something that maybe privileged people talk about with their parents. That leaves a lot of the public without support,” he said.

articles.headline: Firefighters receive 179 reports of people trapped in lifts after sudden voltage dip
articles.dek: Hong Kong firefighters have received over 200 reports of people trapped in lifts and falsely triggered fire alarms after a sudden drop in voltage along a Kowloon power supply line on Tuesday afternoon. CLP Power.
articles.lead: Hong Kong firefighters have received over 200 reports of people trapped in lifts and falsely triggered fire alarms after a sudden drop in voltage along a Kowloon power supply line on Tuesday afternoon.
articles.takeaway: Hong Kong firefighters have received over 200 reports of people trapped in lifts and falsely triggered fire alarms after a sudden drop in voltage along a Kowloon power supply line on Tuesday afternoon.
body: Hong Kong firefighters have received over 200 reports of people trapped in lifts and falsely triggered fire alarms after a sudden drop in voltage along a Kowloon power supply line on Tuesday afternoon.

CLP Power. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Fire Services Department (FSD) said it had handled 179 cases of lift entrapment and 39 false alarms as of 3pm on Tuesday, following a flurry of reports after 1.10pm that was mostly concentrated in Yau Tsim Mong district.

CLP Power, one of the city’s two utility providers, said it detected a “brief yet sudden voltage drop” along a 400-kilovolt power line connecting Lai Chi Kok to Tsz Wan Shan at about 1.09pm on Tuesday, according to local media.

While power supply was not interrupted, the voltage drop might have caused lights to dim or flicker and power-sensitive electronic devices to suspend operation in certain areas of Kowloon and the New Territories, CLP said.
The fire authority received 55 reports of people trapped in lifts and 22 erroneously activated alarms within ten minutes after the voltage drop, according to senior divisional officer Yung Wai-ming.

The Fire Services Department emblem. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Four women aged 68 to 71 reported injuries after being trapped in lifts, Yung said, adding that three of them were sent to hospital in a conscious state, after experiencing discomfort and shortness of breath.

body: Hong Kong police have introduced an artificial intelligence-powered platform designed to educate school pupils about national security. The NSmarties AI Interactive Platform was officially launched on October 6, 2026, at Precious Blood Primary School.

articles.headline: Hong Kong Bus Operators Seek Fare Hikes Up To 17.7% Amid Rising Fuel Costs
articles.dek: Four franchised bus companies have applied for fare increases, citing significant financial pressure from soaring fuel prices exacerbated by the Middle East conflict.
articles.lead: Four franchised bus operators in Hong Kong have applied to raise fares by as much as 17.7 percent, attributing the request to substantial financial strain caused by escalating fuel prices. Citybus is seeking the largest increase at 17.7 percent, while KMB Company has applied for a 16 percent hike. Long Win Bus and New Lantao Bus are requesting increases of 8.1 percent and 9.8 percent, respectively. These applications were submitted to the Transport and Logistics Bureau, which noted that the surge in diesel prices, linked to the Middle East conflict, has placed a significant burden on the operators.
articles.takeaway: Four franchised bus companies have applied for fare increases, citing significant financial pressure from soaring fuel prices exacerbated by the Middle East conflict.
body: Four franchised bus operators in Hong Kong have applied to raise fares by as much as 17.7 percent, attributing the request to substantial financial strain caused by escalating fuel prices. Citybus is seeking the largest increase at 17.7 percent, while KMB Company has applied for a 16 percent hike. Long Win Bus and New Lantao Bus are requesting increases of 8.1 percent and 9.8 percent, respectively. These applications were submitted to the Transport and Logistics Bureau, which noted that the surge in diesel prices, linked to the Middle East conflict, has placed a significant burden on the operators.

The bureau indicated that the fuel purchase prices for these companies saw increases of approximately 75 to 134 percent in March compared to January. This has led to a corresponding rise in fuel expenditure of 85 to 132 percent over the same period. The current geopolitical situation suggests that oil prices are likely to remain elevated.

Despite these pressures, the four companies reported profits ranging from HK$7.92 million to HK$369 million in 2025. However, all are estimated to have experienced a considerable drop in profits during the first half of the current year. For instance, KMB, which carried an average of 2.53 million passengers daily, saw its post-tax profit fall by an estimated 55 percent in the first half of this year.

Citybus, serving an average of 890,000 passengers daily, estimated a 52 percent profit decline for the first half of this year. New Lantao Bus and Long Win Bus, carrying 110,000 and 140,000 passengers daily respectively, estimated profit drops of 129 percent and 31 percent. The bureau acknowledged that the operating environment for bus operators remains challenging due to competition, rising operating costs, and persistent high oil prices.

Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan stated that the government will carefully assess the applications, considering public affordability alongside the service reliability and financial sustainability of the bus companies. Factors such as projected operating costs, revenue, and long-term financial outlook will be examined. The Legislative Council's transport panel is scheduled to discuss these proposals, with final approval resting with the Chief Executive in Council.

articles.dek: A Hong Kong court has imprisoned a former assistant warden for raping an intellectually disabled resident multiple times, with the judge calling the acts 'extremely despicable'.
articles.lead: A former assistant warden at a care home for individuals with intellectual disabilities has been sentenced to 13 years in prison for raping a 23-year-old female resident five times. The assaults occurred between July 13 and August 9, 2024, at the Hong Chi Pinehill Integrated Vocational Training Centre Kwong Fuk Hostel in Tai Po.
articles.takeaway: A Hong Kong court has imprisoned a former assistant warden for raping an intellectually disabled resident multiple times, with the judge calling the acts 'extremely despicable'.
body: A former assistant warden at a care home for individuals with intellectual disabilities has been sentenced to 13 years in prison for raping a 23-year-old female resident five times. The assaults occurred between July 13 and August 9, 2024, at the Hong Chi Pinehill Integrated Vocational Training Centre Kwong Fuk Hostel in Tai Po.

High Court Judge Douglas Yau Tak-hong stated that the defendant, Chung Pui-kei, 38, showed no remorse and was at high risk of reoffending. The judge condemned the assaults as "extremely despicable," highlighting Chung's abuse of his position as a carer and the betrayal of trust placed in him by the employer and the victim's family.

The victim, who has an intellectual developmental disorder equivalent to a nine-year-old's mental capacity, testified that she had refused Chung's advances and expressed discomfort but feared speaking out. The judge noted that Chung's decision to plead not guilty prolonged the victim's ordeal by requiring her testimony.

Chung's defense, which suggested semen found on the victim's bedsheet was transferred through his sleepwear while he slept, was dismissed by the judge as "absurd" and a waste of court time. The jury found Chung guilty of five counts of rape, with the 13-year sentence reflecting the severity of the crimes.

body: Hong Kong’s new Huanggang Port recorded 79,500 passenger movements and 8,000 vehicle movements on its first day of operations, with transport officials preparing for heavier flows expected during the coming holiday weekend.

Statistics from the Shenzhen General Station of Exit and Entry Frontier Inspection showed 41,300 passenger trips entered Hong Kong through the rebuilt checkpoint on Monday, while 38,200 departed the city.
